name: Sentence Connectors
moduleIntroduction: Welcome to the Sentence Connectors module! These are the 'glue' words that hold your ideas together. In French, you can often use the same connector logic (like *pour* or *malgré*), but English is strict! Some connectors demand a Noun (*Because of*), while others demand a Verb (*Because*).
contrastiveExplanation:
Although vs. Despite:
English: 'Although' + Sentence. 'Despite' + Noun.
French: 'Bien que' and 'Malgré' logic is similar, but 'Despite that...' is wrong.

Because vs. Because of:
English: 'Because' + Verb. 'Because of' + Noun.
French: 'Parce que' vs 'À cause de'.

During vs. While:
English: 'During' + Noun. 'While' + Sentence.
French: 'Pendant' covers both.

commonErrors.wrong: Despite he is rich, he is sad.
commonErrors.correct: Although he is rich, he is sad.
commonErrors.frenchConnection: Translating the logic of 'Bien qu'il soit'. 'Despite' cannot touch a subject pronoun (he).
Translating 'Pour' (for) + Infinitive. Use 'To' for purpose with verbs.

commonErrors.wrong: I didn't come because of I was sick.
commonErrors.correct: I didn't come because I was sick.
commonErrors.frenchConnection: Using 'Because of' before a full sentence.

commonErrors.wrong: I slept during the film was playing.
commonErrors.correct: I slept while the film was playing.
commonErrors.frenchConnection: French 'Pendant' covers both. 'During' needs a noun, 'While' needs a verb.
Putting 'also' at the end like French 'aussi'. 'Also' goes before the verb.

items.questionText: I like rice ___ beans.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: J'aime le riz et les haricots...

items.questionText: He is rich, ___ he is not happy.
I was tired, ___ I went to bed.
I stayed home ___ it was raining.
Do you want tea ___ coffee?
He speaks French. He ___ speaks English.
I like mangoes ___.

frenchComparison.whyDifficult: 'Too' goes at the end of the sentence.

items.questionText: It was cold, ___ I wore a jacket.
I studied hard, ___ I failed.
First, I wake up. ___, I brush my teeth.
He is tall ___ strong.
I didn't go ___ I was sick.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Je n'y suis pas allé parce que...

items.questionText: I want to go, ___ I have no money.
___ I was hungry, I ate.
I play football. I ___ play basketball.
Is he Cameroonian ___ Nigerian?
It is raining, ___ take an umbrella.
I like dogs, ___ I don't like cats.
He is smart ___ funny.
___, we went home.
We didn't go ___ the rain.
items.feedback: Correct! 'The rain' is a noun, so we need 'because of'.

items.questionText: ___ he was tired, he kept working.
items.feedback: Correct! Followed by a subject+verb (he was).

items.questionText: He kept working ___ his illness.
I fell asleep ___ the film.
items.feedback: Correct! 'The film' is a noun. Use 'during'.

frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French 'Pendant' is used for both During and While.

items.questionText: I fell asleep ___ I was watching the film.
items.feedback: Correct! Followed by a clause (I was watching).

items.questionText: It was ___ a hot day that we went swimming.

frenchComparison.englishStructure: It was such a hot day...
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: Such + Noun Phrase. French uses 'si' or 'tellement'.

items.questionText: The day was ___ hot that we went swimming.
___ the traffic, I arrived on time.
He is studying ___ pass the exam.

frenchComparison.englishStructure: He is studying in order to pass...
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: In order to + Verb. French uses 'pour'.

items.questionText: He is studying ___ he can pass.

frenchComparison.englishStructure: He is studying so that he can...
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: So that + Clause. French uses 'pour que'.

items.questionText: ___ it rained, we played football.
I didn't buy it ___ it was expensive.
The flight was cancelled ___ the storm.

frenchComparison.whyDifficult: Due to + Noun. Similar to Because of.

items.questionText: I went to the market ___ buy fish.
I went to the market ___ fish.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Je suis allé... pour du poisson...

items.questionText: ___ you study, you will pass.
I will wait ___ you come.
He is rich; ___, he is unhappy.
items.feedback: Correct! Connector at start of new clause.

items.questionText: Both Muna ___ Ngono are here.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Muna et Ngono sont tous deux...

items.questionText: Either you ___ I must go.
___ being tired, he went to work.
In spite of ___ late, he finished the job.
I like football, ___ my brother prefers tennis.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Whereas' shows contrast between two clauses.

items.questionText: ___ my brother, I don't like tennis.
Not only is he rich, ___ he is also famous.
Find the error: "Despite that he is sick, he works."
items.feedback: Correct! 'Despite that' is wrong. Use 'Although he is sick' or 'Despite being sick'.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Malgré qu'il soit malade (often heard but incorrect)...

items.questionText: We must study; ___, we will fail.
You can go ___ you come back early.

frenchComparison.whyDifficult: Provided that + Clause. French 'À condition que'.

items.questionText: ___ had I arrived when the phone rang.
No sooner had I left ___ it started raining.
He has no money. ___, he is happy.
___ the fact that he is old, he runs fast.
___ I agree with you, I can't help you.
items.feedback: Correct! 'While' can mean 'Although' at the start of a sentence.

frenchComparison.whyDifficult: While can mean Although. French 'Bien que'.

items.questionText: I like him ___ he is annoying.
On the one hand, it's cheap. ___ hand, it's ugly.
He didn't study. ___, he failed.
He didn't come ___ his illness.

frenchComparison.whyDifficult: Owing to + Noun. French 'En raison de'.

items.questionText: ___ you study, you won't pass.

frenchComparison.whyDifficult: Unless = If not. French 'À moins que'.
